newsitem.title: JAPAN: Hamanaka trial session to spotlight Sumitomo checks.
newsitem.headline: Hamanaka trial session to spotlight Sumitomo checks.

text.p: Yasuo Hamanaka, the one-time king of the world copper market who has pleaded guilty to fraud and forgery, returns to a court on Monday for a second hearing at which his former employer will be under the spotlight.
Hamanaka, who spent all of his professional life at trading house Sumitomo Corp., was fired last June for what the firm said was a decade of unauthorised trading that cost it $2.6 billion.
He pleaded guilty in a Tokyo court on Feb. 17 to charges of fraud and forgery in connection with the losses. The charges carry a penalty of up to 15 years in prison.
On Monday, the court will get a closer view of internal checks and controls at Sumitomo when its hears testimony from Yoshio Takeuchi of the trade house's credit control department.
Both prosecution and defence sides are expected to question Takeuchi.
"We're going to question him about how exactly Sumitomo's internal checks and controls worked," said Toru Yoshiki, one of the lawyers on Hamanaka's defence team.

Hamanaka was released on bail from a Tokyo Detention Centre on Feb. 24, after spending about four months in jail. He put up bail of 50 million Japanese yen ($409,000), and returned home to the city of Kawasaki on the outskirts of Tokyo.
Until his dismissal, Hamanaka, 49, was known in copper market circles as "Mr Five Percent" as he and his trading team were reckoned to control that proportion of the world's copper trades.
"He is now spending time together with his family and is quietly waiting for the second hearing," Yoshiki said.
Sumitomo's chairman Tomiichi Akiyama resigned his post last Wednesday and was made a special adviser to the firm in a symbolic gesture to atone for the trading losses.
